The three cycle 5 big bets were **Tributary**, **Lantern** and **Hydrant**. The handbook caps each cycle at three big bets, and seven pitches came in [1][2].

- **Tributary:** streaming joins for the Enrich step. Pitched by Mateo and LZ. The cycle scope was CDC-backed snapshots, the editor preview, dead-letter routing and a October private beta with design partners [1]. Private beta started October 1 with eight design partners, and GA stays January 2027. Security sign-off on persisted snapshots is still outstanding and is the main risk [5].
- **Lantern:** self-serve billing portal. Pitched by NH and HV. The original target was a December beta and January 2027 GA, and it depends on the payment-provider migration [1]. The timeline has since slipped: beta is now February 2027 and GA March 2027 [4][5].
- **Hydrant:** automatic per-cell scaling for ingest gateways, pitched by OA. It included the gateway TLS session ticket change from INC-2291 as a small batch item [1]. It shipped to all production cells on October 22, 2026 [3][4].

Pitches that weren't picked are dropped, not carried over, so they must be re-pitched [2]. Tidepool was not picked in cycle 5 and needs a re-pitch with smaller scope, and Bellbuoy is set for re-pitch in cycle 6 [4].

Four endpoints are unavailable on Starter. Calls to them return HTTP 403 rather than the 429 rate-limit response [1].

- `POST /v2/events/batch` (bulk backfill and replays) [1]
- `POST /v2/reference-tables/{id}/refresh` (forces an Enrich snapshot rebuild) [1]
- `GET /v2/audit-log/export` (audit log CSV export) [1]
- `/v2/scim/*` (SCIM user provisioning) [1]

The SCIM endpoints are unavailable on Growth as well, so they are only available on Enterprise [1]. The rate-limit table is the internal source of truth for these limits, last updated October 21, 2026 [1].

|---|---|---|
| `ingest-gateway` | Accepts events from customer SDKs and the HTTP API and writes them to Kafka [1] | DP |

| Conduit | Source and destination connectors (Postgres, MySQL, Snowflake, warehouses) [1] | DP |
| Driftwood | Long-term object archive behind the hot buffer [1] | PLAT |
| Keystone | Authentication and authorization for the app and API [1] | IDB |

Restricted is the highest data class in the information security policy, covering customer event payloads, credentials and encryption keys [3]. Three items are Tier 3, meaning not stocked at any clinic and ordered from the wholesaler for a named patient (allowing 5 business days) [1]:

- **Td** (tetanus-diphtheria), $46 self-pay. Tdap is preferred; Td is only given on request [1].
- **Pneumococcal conjugate PCV21**, $280 self-pay. Only when the clinician specifies PCV21 [1].
- **HPV vaccine, 9-valent**, $295 per dose. Ages 9–45 [1].
- **Meningococcal B vaccine**, $190 per dose. Ages 16–23 or on specialist advice [1].

Tier 2 items (hepatitis B, recombinant zoster, and ceftriaxone) are not stocked at every clinic. They are held only at hub clinics and transferred to other clinics within 2 business days, so they don't need a named-patient order unless the hub is out of stock [1][2].

Under the current standard (effective September 1, 2026), a clinic is large when its average is over 80 visits a day [1]. Based on the July–September 2026 averages in the October 2026 clinic directory, three clinics qualify:

- **Harbor Point (HBP): 118 visits/day** [3]
- **Northgate (NGT): 102 visits/day** [3]
- **Riverside (RVS): 94 visits/day** [3]

Elm Park (85) is in the medium band, since medium is 40 to 80 [1][3]. Elm Park is only five visits above the 80 threshold, so it could move into large if its volume rises. Bands are reset every quarter from this column [1][3].

The 2025 standard used a different threshold (over 90 visits/day), which would have made only Harbor Point and Northgate large [2].

rows.answer:
Five vendors offer 24/7 support that covers P1 problems:

- **Meridian Clinical Systems** (Meridian EHR): 24/7, 15-minute P1 response [1].
- **ClearPath Software** (ClearPath PM): 24/7 for P1 only; other priorities run 07:00–19:00 Eastern, Mon–Fri. P1 response is 30 minutes [1].
- **Coriander Media** (video SDK and hosted media servers): 24/7, 20-minute P1 response [1].
- **Bayline Reference Laboratories** (HL7 results feed into Switchyard): 24/7 interface desk, 30-minute P1 response [1].
- **Polyglen Interpreting** (interpreter operations desk): 24/7, 10-minute P1 response. Its P1 covers an interpreter not connecting at all; slow connections are tracked in the quarterly language access report instead [1].

Vendors without round-the-clock P1 coverage:

- **Larkspur Telehealth**: 07:00–21:00 Eastern, 7 days, 1-hour P1 response [1].
- **Quillon Ambient** (AI scribe pilot): 06:00–22:00 Eastern, Mon–Sat, with no out-of-hours P1 line. Clinicians document manually outside those hours [1].
- **RotaLeaf** (HR and leave system): 08:00–18:00 Eastern, Mon–Fri, 4-hour P1 response [1].

Built-in systems such as Switchyard and Pillbox have no outside vendor. The Service Desk pages the owning team directly for P1 issues [1].
